text:
jamie: deploy bot flagged a burst of failed post-deploy embedding synthetics on embeddings-route in us-central after the 02:10 rollout. sending to eng-releases for quick triage.

deploy-bot: AUTO: postdeploy-synth us-central embeddings-route: 6/12 failures over 3m. canary cohort: 20%. rolling forward paused. first-fail sample ids: [e3a9, b7f2]. logs: /deploy/logs/1765000000/us-central.

nish: copying logs. quick glance shows failed responses with empty embedding vectors (len=0) and 502 from worker pool on the busiest host.

sre-bot: sampler note: error class: worker-noresponse, observed on 2/5 hosts in the pool. network latency OK, CPU/GPU usage normal. KV cache misses minimal. suspect a worker thread deadlock or a process OOM loopback.

carla: can we run the local smoke runner against one failing host and the pinned baseline (embeddings-v1) to compare?

paul: on it. running curl against failing instance:
```
$ curl -s -X POST https://internal.us-central.embed/check -d '{"text":"test"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -i
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"worker_no_response"}
```

paul: baseline pinned model test (embeddings-v1 pinned):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"vector":[0.001, -0.002, ...], "len":1536}
```

nish: that points to a worker-level regression in the new variant. plan suggestion: 1) pause rollout (pin canary to 0%) 2) scale down the new variant instances to isolate, 3) collect core dumps/logs from affected workers, 4) if replicable revert to pinned variant.

jamie: agree. pause and collect. deploy-bot: pause canary and add a temp escalation tag to oncall?

deploy-bot: ACTION: rollout paused by jamie. canary set to 0%. escalation: oncall-high.

sre-bot: adding runbook step: enable higher-fidelity worker logs and set worker_restart_on_hang=true for diagnostic window. Also set synth probe frequency to 8s for 10m to observe stability.

carla: i'm SSHing to the failing host to capture logs and trigger a safe restart of the worker process. command: `sudo systemctl restart r-embed-worker@3`

(60s)

carla: post-restart probe against same host returns 200 and vector length 1536, p95 back to baseline. logs show worker thread hit a rare lock contention during aggressive background checkpoint. core dump captured.

paul: attaching short trace: stack shows background checkpoint holding mutex while main request thread waited -> worker_no_response. filing bug with reproducer steps.

nish: recommendation: revert config in the new variant that enabled async checkpointing until we have a fix. do we want to rollback or patch config and retry canary?

jamie: patch config in canary (disable async checkpoint) and run a small staggered ramp: 2% -> 10% with synth checks. rollback only if we see 3/10 failures.

paul: pushed config change to canary and triggered synthetic runner. initial run: 12/12 success, p95 84ms.

(3 minutes)

nish: after 3m soak with 8s probes, no failures. good to resume gradual rollout with manual gates. follow-ups: - eng-runtime to revert async checkpoint change permanently or make it opt-in behind a flag with health checks (owner: nish) - add worker hang detection to SLOs (sre) - add the reproducer to CI for the variant (carla).

jamie: release note: "Embeddings route: transient worker hang in new variant caused post-deploy synthetic failures in us-central; mitigated by pausing rollout, restarting worker, and disabling async checkpointing in canary. No user-visible impact."

deploy-bot: AUTO: postdeploy-synth resolved. canary at 10% per jamie.

jamie: closing thread. thanks all :white_check_mark:
